title: TrioForge rules file
description: Every model constant of TrioForge, one entry per rule, each with a confidence seal, a list of public sources and a date. Checked by trioforge.rules, which also enforces what a schema cannot: unique ids, calendar-valid dates (format 'date'), strict JSON (no duplicate keys; only finite numbers; integers of at most 15 digits; string keys; no extreme nesting), the shape of curve values (an object with breaks and slopes) and the rule that a rule resting on a private observation keeps digits out of its notes.
$comment: Every pattern in this file ends in (?![\s\S]) and never in $: Python (and some other regex engines) let $ match just before a trailing newline, so 'x.y\n' would pass a pattern that ends in $. (?![\s\S]) is the end of the string in every engine.

version.description: Date of this version of the file.

rules.description: The rules, one object each. Ids are unique across the whole list, superseded rules included.

date.description: A calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. The pattern fixes the shape; format 'date' rejects impossible dates such as 2026-13-01.

settled_value.description: A value that a settled rule (active or superseded) may hold: any JSON value except null. Only an open rule may be waiting for a value.

text.description: A string with at least one non-blank character.

seal.description: How far a rule can be trusted. client: read from a game client file. developer: a developer statement or patch note. measured: our own in-game test or a reproduced stat window. player: several independent player reports. model: our or EQEmu's formula, or a judgment constant.

source_entry.description: One place a value comes from. url: a public https address. client-file: a text resource that ships with the game client, read as text. public-text: a public statement without a stable address, such as a patch note or a developer stream. private-measured and private-player: the maintainer's own measurement, or player reports the maintainer saw privately; the ref is then one fixed label and never a count, value or date.

kind.description: What sort of place the ref names.

ref.description: What the kind points at. url: an https:// address (a host, then an optional path; no spaces, user name or port). client-file: one of the shipped text files listed below. public-text: a short description. private-measured and private-player: exactly "maintainer's private observation".

not.$comment: Nothing public may cite a client binary, an address or offset inside it, or a disassembly (the game's terms rule out reverse engineering the client): no eqgame, .exe, RVA, offset or 0x. Written with character classes because JSON Schema patterns have no case-insensitive flag. RVA stays case-sensitive on purpose: its lowercase form sits inside ordinary words, such as 'observation' in the fixed private label.

allOf.$comment: (?![\s\S]) is the end of the string in every regex engine, where $ also matches before a trailing newline in some of them.
Only text resources that ship with the game client, read as text. Never a binary.
A private observation is cited by one fixed label, so no count, value or date of the maintainer's logs or stat windows can reach the public file.

sources.description: Where a value comes from: a non-empty list of source entries.

alternative.description: A competing value for a rule, kept next to the chosen one with its own seal and sources.

value.description: Any JSON value. A curve (breaks and slopes) is checked like the value of a rule.

id.description: Dotted lowercase identifier, unique in the file.

title.description: Short human-readable name, shown next to the value.

value.description: Any JSON value. null means 'no value yet' and is only legal for open rules (see the second allOf entry below). An object with both breaks and slopes is a piecewise-linear curve; trioforge.rules checks that it has one more slope than breaks, that the breaks strictly increase and that every slope is a finite number.

unit.description: What the value counts or measures (free text, for display).

source.description: Where the value comes from: a non-empty list of public sources (a URL, a shipped client text file, a public statement) and, where the maintainer's own observation also backs the value, the fixed private label.

date.description: Date of the evidence behind the value.

status.description: active: in use. open: waiting for an in-game test to settle it. superseded: replaced, kept for history, never returned by lookups.

levels.description: Overrides of value by character level: an object from a level string to the value at that level. A level is a whole number from 1 to 99 written without a leading zero, such as "55". Like value, a level value is null only on an open rule.

test.description: The in-game test that will settle the rule, such as B4. Required when status is open.

notes.description: Free-text remarks. When the rule or one of its alternatives has a private-measured or private-player source, the notes hold no digit at all (no counts, values or dates); trioforge.rules checks that.

alternatives.description: Competing values, each with its own seal and sources.

allOf.$comment: An open rule is waiting for an in-game test, so it must say which one.

null means 'no value yet', which only an open rule may have, in value and in every level value alike. There is no exception: a finding such as 'there is no cap' is written as a value (the string "none"), not as null.
